stem: Trihalomethanes are organic molecules in which three of the hydrogen atoms of methane are replaced by halogen atoms, for example $\text{CHF}_3$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The equation shows a reaction to produce $\text{CHF}_3$.

$$\text{CHI}_3\text{(s)} + 3\text{AgF}\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{CHF}_3\text{(g)} + 3\text{AgI}\text{(s)}$$

Use the data to calculate the enthalpy change of reaction, $\Delta H_{\text{r}}$, for this formation of $\text{CHF}_3$.

| compound | enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}/\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{CHI}_3\text{(s)}$ | -182.1 |
| $\text{CHF}_3\text{(g)}$ | -692.9 |
| $\text{AgF}\text{(s)}$ | -204.6 |
| $\text{AgI}\text{(s)}$ | -61.8 |

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
The graph shows the relationship between $pV$ and $p$ at a given temperature for $\text{CHF}_3$ and an ideal gas.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
$\text{CHF}_3$ is not an ideal gas.

State **three** basic assumptions that scientists make about the properties of ideal gases.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why $\text{CHF}_3$ deviates from the properties of an ideal gas at pressures greater than 300 atm.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
A different trihalomethane, $\text{CHCl}_3$, reacts with $\text{O}_2$ to produce carbonyl dichloride. $\text{HCl}\text{(g)}$ is also released as a product of this reaction.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation for this reaction of $\text{CHCl}_3$ with $\text{O}_2$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The conversion of $\text{CHCl}_3$ to carbonyl dichloride can be monitored by infra-red spectroscopy. The infra-red spectrum of carbonyl dichloride is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}

On the infra-red spectrum of carbonyl dichloride identify with an **X** the absorption that would **not** be present in an infra-red spectrum of $\text{CHCl}_3$.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest another difference between the infra-red spectra of $\text{CHCl}_3$ and carbonyl dichloride.
